record_type_quote: In this study, we selected five SNPs (rs1801274 in FCGR2A locus, rs2286672 in PLD2 locus, rs887369 in CXorf21 locus, rs9782955 in LYST , and rs3794060 in NADSYN1 ) that were identified to be associated with SLE from a previous GWAS [ 12 ] but have not been tested in a Korean population.

targets.authors: Bentham J, Morris DL, Cunninghame Graham DS, Pinder CL, Tombleson P, Behrens TW, et al.
targets.title: Genetic association analyses implicate aberrant regulation of innate and adaptive immunity genes in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus.
targets.evidence_quote: Recently, Bentham et al. [ 12 ] performed a large-scale GWAS with 7,219 cases and 15,991 controls in Europeans and defined 43 SLE loci, including 10 new loci. Among the SLE-associated loci in Bentham et al. [ 12 ], some of them have not been replicated in the Korean population, and others were replicated but not concluded to be associated due to a limited sample size. In this study, we aimed to replicate five SNPs that were not replicated or concluded to be association in Koreans.
targets.outcome_quote: Through a replication study with 656 cases and 622 controls, rs1801274 in FCGR2A was found to be significantly associated with SLE in Koreans. However, the other four candidate SNPs were not replicated in Koreans.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly confirm one of the five tested associations and report that the other four did not replicate. All five are selected from the single Bentham et al. original; other studies discussed for context are not separately re-tested.

reasoning: New Korean case and control samples re-test five published associations from Bentham et al. (2015). Identity verified by title, DOI, and the three authors on the full publisher article.
